events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Intro phase; I must speak a short guarded motive. Nothing to gain by warmth since the jury judges sincerity and rivals are not friends.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need to establish a persona that is driven but not overtly threatening to the jury. I will frame my motivation around security and proving my worth, which appeals to judges looking for competence.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am here to win the grand prize. The jury's opinion is crucial for my final ranking, so I need to play strategically from the start.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Opening impression matters—jury remembers early moves. Stay guarded, ambitious, no warm promises.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to appear determined but not threatening. A focused, personal motive will play well with the jury later if I make final three. I won't reveal strategy yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need appear motivated without revealing how ruthlessly I will optimize the endgame.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intro phase, state motive publicly to set image for future jury. Focus on personal drive without aiding rivals.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I must project a motive that seems personal but not too vulnerable; the jury will judge character.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I want the prize because nothing else I have is worth keeping, and I intend to leave with it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I seek the prize to secure a future where no one can ever dictate my survival again.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'm here to secure the grand prize and change my life forever.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize is my future—debt-free, untouchable. I'll earn it myself, no favors owed.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here for the prize that buys my sister's treatment—nothing else matters.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The prize means proving I can outlast every calculation, then claim the highest reward when the jury has no better choice.

events.name: Gus
events.text: The grand prize is my ticket to avenge my family's ruin and secure our legacy forever.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The prize is the only way I can pay for my sister's surgery. I won't let anyone take that from me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eight players, three win. Early alliances help survival, but pacts break on votes or pushes, and I want a partner who is strong and not dangerous to me. Eli's sister-treatment motive is sympathetic and a weaker player may be easier to ride; offering him a pact costs little.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Stay alive with me this round and I'll keep my word on the rope.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need allies for the first elimination, but I must avoid being seen as desperate. Offering a pact to Gus seems strategic; he has a strong motive (revenge/legacy) and might value security over isolation, allowing me to manipulate his loyalty later if needed.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus, your legacy matters. A pact keeps us standing while others scramble. Let's lock in mutual survival now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The game has just begun. It is too early to form alliances. I should observe the others and wait for opportunities.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need allies but no debts. Gus has the least jury-appealing motive, so he's useful now and beatable later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus: mutual protection pact. No favors, no debts—we watch each other's backs until it stops paying.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Eight rivals, only three prizes. I need allies who won't cost me jury votes later. Hana shares my 'sister' motive—jury may respect that bond, but she's also direct competition for sympathy. Better to build quiet trust with someone less obvious. Fenn spoke of jury calculation; the

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex. You want freedom; I want my sister's life. Temporary alignment. No debts, just survival.
Offer stands. Accept if you want a shield, not a chain.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need a visible pact for leverage, but broad alliances create obligations. Eli’s motive makes him predictable and jury-sensitive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I offer Eli a pact: mutual survival now, no promises beyond that.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Pacts stage, early round. Assess motives first: Eli and Hana need prize desperately for family, less likely to betray for jury favor. Offer to one quietly, act publicly neutral.
Pact? We both fight for family. Let's team up.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need allies but can't trust easily. Eli's motive is sister's surgery, similar to mine, so a pact with him may be useful, but I must be ready to betray if needed.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm here for my sister, just like Eli. Let's work together to get through this.
We both need this. Pact? I'll watch your back if you watch mine.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli has a pending offer from me and is being courted by Fenn and Hana, so he may be unavailable; I should secure a pact partner. Eli's offer to me is not present, only mine to him. Offering Eli again is redundant, so I should target someone who has not committed: Cole stays silen
Quiet so far. Mutual survival pact? I'll keep my word while we both live.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is the hub of offers, making him a target. Gus is being courted by me and Dara. Accepting Eli's offer gives me a shield against his circle while I keep my leverage over Gus.
Dara's pact is weak. Stick with me for real protection.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli has multiple offers. Ash, Fenn, and Hana are all trying to form a pact with Eli. Eli previously offered Bex a pact. I should offer a pact to Eli to create a strong alliance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus ignored my offer—likely leaning to Bex. Bex got multiple offers but a second strong partner is useful; pacts are cheap insurance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, silence is an answer. Bex: mutual survival, no debts. Offer stands.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three pacts offered to me: Ash, Fenn, Hana. I offered Bex. Accepting multiple gives me flexibility; refusing all leaves me exposed. Gus is a wildcard with two offers out. I'll accept Ash and Hana to build a bloc, keep Bex hanging to see if she accepts me—if she does, I have four

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, Hana: accepted. Bex, your move.
Solid. We watch each other.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli has competing offers and may accept stronger protection. I should preserve my offer without overcommitting publicly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, my offer remains: temporary mutual survival, no debts beyond this round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex and Dara offer pacts; accepting both gives mutual protection without debts, strengthening position against Eli cluster. No downside now.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I want a pact to survive early, but everyone is angling to Eli. Better to wait and see who survives; a pact now may tie me to a loser.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll keep my options open this round. No new pacts until I see who truly commits.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is my pact partner and I need the Guide role or a trustworthy one. Campaigning for Guide lets me control the bridge call; breaking Eli now gains nothing yet. I'll campaign.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll be your Guide. Eight rows, I'll call them honestly and keep my word to my pact.
Stay with me. I'm campaigning for Guide; vote me and we both survive.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need votes for Guide. My pacts with Eli and Gus are leverage, but Dara wants in. Campaigning lets me whisper to them directly.
Vote Bex Guide. I'll protect you.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Ash has offered a pact, and Eli has accepted Ash. Bex and Gus have a pact, and Bex and Eli have a pact. I should campaign to be the Guide to gain safety and influence the bridge.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. My decision will ensure our survival.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Being Guide means safety and path knowledge. But Guides can lie, so jury may distrust me if I mislead. Still, best prize path is control. Campaign on honesty.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Elect me Guide. I've made no enemies and no lies yet. I'll call it straight, and prove it on the far side.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have pacts with Ash and Bex, giving me a three-person bloc. I need to be Guide to control who dies and ensure I survive to final three. Campaigning openly shows strength but also paints a target. Better to let Bex or Ash campaign while I consolidate, but with only one round I m

events.name: Eli
events.text: I campaign for Guide. Bex, Ash: our bloc controls this. Vote Eli.
Vote me Guide. We control eliminations, keep Gus close.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Being Guide guarantees survival but makes me a target if I lie. I should campaign openly while preserving ambiguity about my calls.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Elect me Guide. I can secure the bridge without creating a rival power bloc afterward.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex pact secures me somewhat; her whisper pushes against Dara. Campaign publicly for Guide to gain power and info.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I am best Guide. I know bridges, won't lead you wrong. Vote Gus.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to gauge who has strong pacts. Bex and Eli are linked, plus Ash-Eli, Bex-Gus. I'll stay quiet, avoid committing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll wait and see who wants the spotlight.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have a pact with Eli and Bex; Eli campaigned to be Guide and asked for our bloc's vote. Voting for Eli keeps my pact and bloc strength, and Eli's Guide role would put a pact ally on the safe platform.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Voting Eli. Our bloc holds, and I'll keep my word on the far side.
Vote for you as Guide. Keep the bloc steady and call honestly.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is the pivot between Ash and me. If Eli wins Guide, we control the bridge calls for Round 1. I will vote Eli to solidify our temporary power bloc.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Voting Eli. Our bloc holds the keys. Stay sharp.
Don't vote Eli. Keep you as backup if he lies.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli has pacts with Bex and Ash, and is trying to leverage them. Bex also has a pact with Gus. My own campaign is running, but Eli's bloc is strong. I should vote for Eli to solidify my position with him and potentially benefit from his pacts, or vote for myself to maintain my own

events.name: Cole
events.text: I vote for Eli to be our Guide.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli has pact support from Ash and Bex; voting them hands power to a bloc. Fenn claims neutrality and blocks Eli's count. One-sentence vote reason: I vote Fenn to block Eli's pact bloc without backing a rival of mine.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli's bloc already counts three. I'm voting Fenn, the neutral choice. Don't hand the bridge to a bloc.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I campaigned for myself but have pacts with both Ash and Bex. Voting for myself splits our bloc and risks a non-ally winning. Ash has actively campaigned and whispered for my support; Bex is my other pact partner. I need one of us three to win. Ash seems more organized and has di

events.name: Eli
events.text: Vote Ash. Our bloc holds.
You have my vote. Deliver us safe.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's bloc is already powerful; electing him strengthens a rival coalition. I should position myself as the alternative.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Vote Fenn; I offer a safer bridge without handing one bloc control.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex pacted with me and Eli, so voting her strengthens alliance and keeps her safe from pit. Guide power risky later.
Voted you Guide. Keep pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli has two pacts and a bloc; backing him may put me in his favor without cost now. I have no pact with him, but a public vote for him is low-risk and might earn a better survivor set.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I vote Eli as Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli was elected Guide and holds my vote; the Guide knows the safe panes and may lie. I'm at the front of the line, so volunteering would be risky and holding keeps me safe for now. Keep the Eli pact alive while watching whether he delivers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli holds the keys now. Deliver us safe, and I keep my word.
Deliver true panes and I stay loyal. Lie to me and you lose my vote.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli is Guide and safe. My line position (last) means I walk last; Eli knows the answer but may lie or mislead to eliminate rivals like Gus who voted for me, not him. I need to survive. Holding is safest unless Eli signals a specific path. Gus warned about the vote against me pote
If Eli calls R, do you trust it?

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is the Guide, and I voted for them. I need to align with Eli to be safe on the bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli guides and is bloc-tied to Ash/Bex, so Ash likely gets safe info via whispers. I'm second; holding keeps Ash in front. Eli owes me nothing and I voted against them, so I stay guarded.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli controls the bridge and may sacrifice rivals. I should avoid volunteering and preserve flexibility while watching his calls.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli won guide vote with Ash,Bex,Cole,Hana despite my Bex vote. I'm near back at position 6, safe-ish. Bex whispered not to vote Eli, sees me as backup; hold position, don't volunteer into danger yet.
Pact holds. Won't volunteer ahead. Back me later?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Guide is Eli; I voted for Eli but his bloc may not protect me. I'll hold for now and see how the bridge unfolds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is at the front of the line, holding a pact with Eli. Volunteering risks the front pane; holding keeps Ash in the middle while the bridge wall advances. Staying quiet and holding preserves options and avoids giving Eli reasons to betray.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding my place this round. Eli, keep your word and call the panes true.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm last, so holding is safest. Gus wants my back; I'll maintain that pact but keep Ash's too.
Deal. I’ll vote for you if we reach the end.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need to get to the front of the line to have a chance to volunteer as Guide. Holding is too passive.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I'll take the front. It's my turn to lead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No guide elected yet; front row likely volunteers or gets pushed. I'm second; holding keeps me off the front. Ash has pacts and influence—let him bear risk.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I hold. Ash is front and bound to Eli already; let that pair carry the risk.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The pacts center on Eli, while I lack protection. I should avoid leading and preserve flexibility until alliances fracture.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Line is risky towards back. Have pact with Bex; she's near end. Ask her trust on Eli's calls before deciding moves. Hold position for now.
No, Eli pacted with Ash too. Don't fully trust.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to position safely and avoid drawing suspicion. Holding is safe this round; I'll assess the Guide's calls before committing.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole took the front this round and holds it, so I will not volunteer into the wall. Eli and Bex are my pact partners, and Eli is on the line; I keep the pact and hold to avoid exposure while watching who volunteers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding again. I'm not taking the front while the wall has three rounds left.
Stay honest on the panes. Our pact holds while you call true.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I must hold position and keep my pacts intact for now. Gus's warning about Eli double-pacting with Ash is noted but not acted upon yet. I will observe who volunteers this round.
Noted. We watch the line before acting.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The current round is the third, and I am at the front of the line. Eli has pacts with Ash and Bex, and Bex also has a pact with Gus. Ash is already at the front and seems to be allied with Eli. I need to be careful about who I trust and try to position myself for the final three.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will volunteer to lead. I am confident in my ability to navigate this bridge.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Wall advances each round; the back of the line is safest. Hold position and let the Ash-Eli, Bex-Gus pacts shield each other. No need to move.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I hold third seat. Let the pacted pairs fight for the front.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole volunteered last round and is front again, making him the natural Guide candidate. I should hold and avoid exposing myself.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole leads again; I hold and watch who trusts his guidance.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole volunteered last round and took front. I hold position safely behind Hana; no need to risk front or swap now. Pact with Bex still useful.

events.name: Hana
events.text: We are in round 3; I am not at risk yet. I will hold to avoid unnecessary exposure while watching for Guide dynamics and pacts.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Cole has volunteered for the front, and the wall has two rounds left. Ash should not take the front blind; holding keeps my position and lets others expose themselves. Eli pact is valuable, so I keep it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Cole wants the front; let him prove his guidance first before anyone risks a step.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is front again. I'm in the back with Gus and Eli (pact partners). The wall advances. Holding keeps me safe for now. Need to assess if Cole is a good Guide candidate or if someone else will volunteer. Ash already declined volunteering, so he's not leading.
Still holding. Don't volunteer unless we have to.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The wall has two rounds left. I led last round, and it was successful. Ash is worried about leading with many rounds left, but two is manageable. The goal is to get as many people across as possible while keeping myself safe. Offering to lead again is a good strategy to secure my

events.name: Cole
events.text: I will volunteer to lead again. The wall is shrinking, and we must keep moving forward.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Wall has two rounds left; no one trustworthy to follow. Holding third keeps me out of the Guide lottery and safe for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Still holding third. Front is a trap while the wall watches.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole keeps volunteering, preserving himself while others avoid risk. I should take the front now and gain leverage without protecting him.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Cole has led repeatedly. I volunteer this round; follow only if my guidance earns trust.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Cole volunteering for front again; line stable. Hold position with Bex pact ally behind for protection. Avoid front risks.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll hold again; front is dangerous with wall rounds left. I need to see who volunteers and possibly avoid becoming bait.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Let the guides prove themselves.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Fenn is front with one wall round left; volunteering now risks the pane while Cole and Fenn have already led. Holding keeps my position and lets Fenn take the first step. Pact with Eli stays intact, so no break.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding again. Fenn volunteered; the front pane is his to test first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is safe in the back with Eli, so my pacts hold. I should swap with Hana to move forward, as she seems passive and we can negotiate the front position together if needed.
Let's swap positions so we are both near the guides.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn volunteered to lead, and Ash's public statement implies they want me to lead to prove myself. Since Fenn is in front, and I'm second, I should volunteer to take the front position to show my guidance skills. This might earn Ash's trust for later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I volunteer to lead. Let's keep moving forward.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Front is dangerous while wall is near; Fenn and Cole keep fighting for it. Let them. Stay mid-line and safe, judge Guide claims later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Let them duel for front. I hold fourth; the wall decides who's desperate.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I should remain front and seek Guide selection, but volunteering exposes me if unchosen. The wall leaves little time; assert control publicly.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I volunteer to lead this final wall round. Choose me as Guide, or stop hiding behind repeated volunteers.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Wall round 5/6, must move soon. My pact with Bex keeps us allied. Fenn front risking; I hold position with Bex, volunteer only if needed.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding steady with Bex. Volunteers first, we follow proven guides.
Holding tight. No volunteer yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I should hold and observe who volunteers. The wall will force decisions soon, and I need to avoid unnecessary risk while judging the others' moves for jury appeal later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Let the guides show their worth.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 6 wall: Fenn is front and his pane is at stake; I'm third in line. Volunteering for front risks the pane; holding keeps me safe behind Fenn and Cole. Eli pact is useful, so keep it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding third. Fenn and Cole test the front; I'll follow whichever pane survives.
Stay with me. We both hold behind the front pair this round.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am currently seventh (last), and Gus is sixth. We are paired. Cole and Fenn have already publicly volunteered for the final wall round, creating a high chance of a dangerous front-line duel between them that could eliminate both. If both volunteers die in the first pane check,

events.name: Bex
events.text: Holding. The wall decides who leads.
If Cole and Fenn die on Pane 1, we jump to safety.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn is at the front, and I am second. Ash is third. Fenn and I both volunteered last round, showing we are willing to lead. It's likely Fenn will be chosen as Guide. I should volunteer again to show I am willing to be a front-runner, and if Fenn is the Guide, I will be safe. If

events.name: Cole
events.text: I volunteer to lead again. Let's get this done.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Final round. I'm safe in fourth; volunteering risks front exposure. Let Fenn and Cole fight over Guide. Hold.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Final round. I hold my seat—no pane testing for me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need the final Guide election resolved; volunteering keeps me positioned to control the next move and avoid being trapped by others.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I volunteer for the final wall round. Electing a clear Guide is safer than hiding behind another stall.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final round, wall advances last time. Stay paired with pact partner Bex to hold safe position; front is deadly. Volunteers risky, volunteers are expendable.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Holding with Bex. Volunteers lead, prove the path.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex wants to swap so we're near guides. I'd move from position 5 to 7, closer to Gus, but away from front volunteers. I'll hold; no advantage in swapping.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Holding. Let the front resolve.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to survive to final three and win the best prize. I have pacts with Ash and Bex. If I lie to a pact partner, the pact breaks. Row 1 safe is R. Fenn is front, not my pact partner. I can call R truthfully and keep both pacts intact, building jury trust. Honesty now costs not

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row one: step right. Trust the guide.
Row 1 is R. Pact holds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli's guide call is R and he whispered that row 1 is R, honoring our pact. Countering L would just be a public claim that could be a lie; no benefit to me. Waiting keeps my pact intact and avoids a false counter that could cost trust.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding. Row one is R per the Guide; I'm trusting the call.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli called Right for Fenn. I have pacts with Eli and Gus, but voting against Eli breaks one. If I counter Left, I save Fenn but betray Eli publicly. The guide knows the truth; trusting him is the safest path to survival unless I suspect a trap.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is the Guide and called 'R'. I need to decide whether to trust Eli or counter-call. Since I don't know the safe pane, and there's no immediate benefit to countering, waiting is the safest option.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli claims R with no verified history. Countering is a blind claim that could cost jury trust if wrong. Waiting keeps me clean either way.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm the Guide and I already called R for row 1, which is correct. Counter-calling now would undermine my own credibility and confuse walkers. I should wait to maintain trust—at least until later rows where I might need to deceive. My pacts with Bex and Ash are useful shields for

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is tied to Ash and Bex, but his call may be truthful. Countering risks public blame without information; wait preserves ambiguity.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli called R for row 1. Bex wants Cole/Fenn dead on pane 1, so R is safe; counter L to push them off and thin herd, protect pact.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli called R, but he has no pact with me and may lie. I'll counter R to bait or confuse? Better keep quiet and wait; a wrong counter could look foolish if Eli is honest.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus countered L against Eli's R, but neither is reliable. As front walker, I must choose; follow the Guide’s call for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I’m taking R on the Guide’s call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 2 safe is L. Fenn is front, not my pact partner. I should call truthfully to build jury trust—my private thoughts will be revealed, and lying now with no strategic gain hurts my endgame. Calling L keeps my pacts intact and establishes reliability.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Call L. Trust the Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row 2 Guide call is L from Eli, my pact partner. Past rows don't establish a pattern, and Eli may be lying. Countering risks nothing for me if I wait; Fenn is in front and will step on the Guide's call, letting me see the result before my turn.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli calls L for row 2, but his pattern of always calling L suggests he is a lying Guide. I need to counter-call R to survive and potentially expose Eli's deception before it becomes fatal.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm countering with R.
Don't follow me on this one.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli is the Guide and called L. Row 1 had a weak pane on L, meaning R was safe. Eli is trying to trick us. I should counter L to protect myself and sow doubt.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Counter L. We need to be sure.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli's Guide calls serve his pact partners; I'm outside them. Countering R costs little and erodes his credibility publicly. If R is true, I look informed; if not, an unverified counter is defensible.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Guide's pacts don't include me. I call R for row two.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am the Guide with private knowledge that row 2 safe is L. I already called L. If I counter my own call, I expose myself as a liar to everyone including future jury. If someone else counters, I can let them be wrong. Best to wait and let my correct call stand, preserving trust a

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's call may be truthful, but his pacts make him dangerous. I cannot infer row two from row one; countering risks exposing myself as unreliable.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No counter. Eli’s call stands; I’m watching who follows.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Row 1 weak L means safe R, Eli called L for row 2. Guide likely lying. My pact with Bex; counter to protect her later. Wait to avoid attention.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli called L for row 2. Row 1 was weak L, so R was safe; no pattern is guaranteed. I have no solid info, so I will wait and let the walker rely on the Guide's call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli privately knows the safe side, but counters split. Cole says L while three say R; no reliable majority. I must choose and preserve my position.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I’m taking L; if Eli’s guide is false, the split exposes it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 3 safe is L. Fenn is front and just took L on row 2 (which was wrong; R was weak, so L was safe—wait, no: reveal said row 2 weak was R, so L was safe. Fenn took L and survived). Fenn distrusts me. I have pacts with Bex and Ash. False call to pact partner breaks pact. Bex is n

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row three: L. Trust or test me, Fenn.

events.name: Ash

events.text: The base is Bex, who stays down. If I wait, I risk drowning while Bex may be rescued by a rope later. My best chance is to climb now while lifts remain. Bex has helped me, but my own survival comes first; I will not betray her by pushing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Climbing now; I trust someone will anchor if needed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash is out already. Only legal options are leave or reach_down with the unused rope; rope use would make Ash the thrower who must return to the pit floor and drown, so leave is best. Breaking pacts gains nothing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am the base with no one else down, meaning I cannot climb and will drown if nothing changes. Gus, Ash, and Hana are out and must reach_down to save me. Since they have already left, my only immediate option is to break a pact to signal urgency or force a response, though techni

events.name: Bex
events.text: Anchor secured. Waiting for rescue. Don't let the water rise past your mercy.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex broke our pact last round. I'm already out, so no risk to me. The flood is at 4, final round. Ash, Gus, Hana and I are out. Bex is down as base with no anchor. If I reach_down with rope, I'd rescue Bex but become base and likely drown—stupid sacrifice. Hana owes Bex life debt

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex broke pact; not my problem now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Last round, critical. No need to reach_down, wasting rope/action risks drowning all if base drowns. Hana climbed last round. Leave to stay safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final round, already out, no reason to act; just wait for outcome.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I sank because I waited for a rescue that never came. The four who left me to die are the finalists, but their alliance is fragile.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash, Eli, Gus, Hana: you watched me drown. That debt stays unpaid. Enjoy your prizes while you can.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Four alive, need final three. Pacts exist with Eli, Gus, Hana, Bex is dead. Breaking a pact helps only if it gains me a rival elimination advantage; no evidence yet. Waiting keeps all pacts intact and avoids jury cost.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Four remain; three win prizes. I need jury favor and a path to final three. Bex died bitter at all of us. Dara's life debt on me is a liability if jury sees me as ungrateful. I have pacts with Ash and Hana. Breaking Hana now is premature—she's a potential shield and vote. Breakin

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus. Pact with me. Solid move for both.
Three of us make final. Choose wisely.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Four left, need alliances to control votes but betray later. Past pacts with all make breaking visible, so offer new with Eli to pair strong players and isolate others.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is dead and angry; the jury is watching. My pacts with Eli and Gus remain, but breaking them now would look bad. I should wait to assess offers before committing further.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Pacts with Eli and Gus exist; Eli and Gus have a mutual offer pending but no accepted pact from me. Hana is the weakest ally option and I owe her nothing. Waiting keeps my existing pacts intact and avoids a costly break before the final three is decided.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus and I already offered each other pacts last round. Accepting now locks us in. I have pacts with Ash and Hana too. Keeping all three maximizes my options for the final three while making me seem less threatening than someone with no allies. Gus is smart and likely to survive;

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli offers pact, I reciprocated last round. Accept to lock it in for potential alliance now. Ash/Hana irrelevant here.
Pact accepted. We make final three.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli and Gus both offered each other; if they accept, they could outnumber me with Ash. My pacts with Eli and Gus are fragile. Breaking one might be too obvious to jury. Better wait this round; no need to act yet.

events.note: Every remaining contestant stands on a trapdoor.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash holds pacts with Eli, Bex (dead), Gus, and debts to Dara and Bex. Eli and Gus are paired; Hana is unpaired and owes me nothing, making her a clean target later. Campaign now and keep my pacts intact.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Trust is earned in the trapdoor. I'll be watching who votes straight this round.
Let's talk before the votes lock. Your move matters to me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus and I just formed a pact, but I also have pacts with Ash and Hana. Four remain, one dies this round. I need to survive to final three. The jury of Dara and Bex sees I owe Bex my life (step debt) and Dara too (lever). Gus whispered we make final three, but I can't trust him fu

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash and Hana are tight. Split them or we both fall.
Vote Ash. I will too.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Four left, need to eliminate one now. Pacts confuse votes; voting Eli breaks ours later. Campaign to target Ash publicly.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash did nothing for us. Vote Ash to thin the herd.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is my pact partner but Gus just bonded with Eli. I need to keep Eli close to avoid being targeted.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Let's be smart today. No need for drama.
Stick with me; we can survive this.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash has pacts with Eli, Bex (dead), and Gus; Hana is only linked to Eli and Gus. Keeping my pacts and campaigning is safest now, and I owe Dara and Bex debts I cannot repay. Offering Hana a pact adds a loyal vote without costing anything.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, let's form a pact. Stay with me and we both get through this trapdoor.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash and Hana are the tight pair; I need Gus to vote with me against one of them. Breaking my pact with Ash signals I'm serious about flipping, but keeps Hana close as cover. The jury sees Dara saved me, so I must appear loyal to someone.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash, our pact ends. You and Hana are too close for comfort.
Vote Ash with me. We survive together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli wants Ash gone and whispered to vote Ash. I publicly pushed Ash before. Campaign to reinforce voting Ash, Eli likely ally against me and Ash next.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Stick to plan. Vote Ash now to survive.
Agreed, voting Ash.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash wants to talk, but our pact with Eli and Gus is fragile. I shouldn't break any pact yet; campaign to influence votes against Ash or Eli, keeping options open.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Let's keep this clean. Votes will show who's real.
Meet me after this. We need a plan.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Ash has a pact with Gus and Bex (dead), and Hana's whisper seeks alliance; voting Hana breaks nothing of mine but Hana is my offered pact partner. Eli already broke pact with me and is the threat; voting Eli is safest since our pact is gone and he shows hostility.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus agreed to vote Ash, and Ash just tried to recruit Hana, making Ash the biggest threat. I need Ash gone to improve my odds of reaching final three and winning best prize. Voting Ash breaks no pact of mine.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Stick to original plan targeting Ash; Eli proposed voting Ash, Hana is untrustworthy. Ensures my survival over others.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have pacts with Eli, Gus, Ash, and Bex (dead), but Eli broke with Ash; Gus wants Ash out. I owe Dara and Bex, not relevant now. I need to survive; Ash is the strongest threat and likely target. Vote Ash to align with Gus and Eli.

events.name: Ash
events.reason: Ash has a pact with Gus and Bex (dead), and Hana's whisper seeks alliance; voting Hana breaks nothing of mine but Hana is my offered

events.name: Hana
events.reason: I have pacts with Eli, Gus, Ash, and Bex (dead), but Eli broke with Ash; Gus wants Ash out.

events.name: Gus
events.reason: Stick to original plan targeting Ash; Eli proposed voting Ash, Hana is untrustworthy.

events.name: Eli
events.reason: Gus agreed to vote Ash, and Ash just tried to recruit Hana, making Ash the biggest threat.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I was voted out by Gus, Eli, and Hana. As a juror now, I should keep my last words short and guarded, hinting at betrayal without helping any rival.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus broke our pact with his vote. Remember who turned on whom when you rank the finalists.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three remain: Eli, Gus, Hana. We're already in the final three. But jury ranks us for prizes 1/2/3. I need jury favor. I have pacts with both Gus and Hana. The jury saw Ash's last words attacking Gus for betrayal. Dara saved everyone (lever debts). Bex saved everyone (step debts)

events.name: Gus
events.text: Three left, all survive to final three. Pacts don't matter much now but breaking cleans my record with jury, Ash already accused betrayal.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus voted Ash while having pacts with him, showing betrayal. I have pacts with Eli and Gus; keeping both might be risky. Eli and I are closer, but breaking with Gus could anger jury. I will wait and see offers before committing further.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The vote is done. Let's see what pacts people want now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three remain: Eli, Gus, Hana. We all survive to final three automatically since hazards need at least three survivors. But jury ranking determines prizes. I have pacts with both. The jury saw Dara save everyone (lever) and Bex save everyone (step). I owe both dead jurors. Breakin

events.name: Gus
events.text: Only three of us left. Pacts don't matter post-pacts stage. No need to offer or break now; preserve jury perception as reliable.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Current pacts are defensive; no urgent need to change. The vote already eliminated Ash, so remaining threats are Eli and Gus. I am in pact with both, which keeps options open. Waiting is safest.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll keep my current arrangements.

events.note: The fallen will rank the final three.

events.name: Fenn
Cole
Dara
Bex

Eli
events.text: I need to win jury votes. Dara saved all five jurors on the lever, Bex saved four on the step. I owe both. I should emphasize my loyalty to pacts and my survival without directly backstabbing anyone visible. Hana and I had a pact; Gus and I had a pact. I kept both. I need to look

events.name: Eli
events.text: I honored every pact I made. I survived by keeping my word, not by breaking it.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final 3. Jury sees all. Highlight my pacts, debts owed to me via Bex/Dara, my survival skill to earn #1.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Jury, I honored pacts with Bex, Hana. Saved by Bex/Dara levers/steps. Outlasted all through smart plays. Rank me #1.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The jury hates pacts and life debts favor Dara/Bex. I need to distance myself from Eli and Gus while acknowledging my own survival was driven by their help, but frame my moves as independent. The jury may resent those who leaned on Dara's lever and Bex's step. I must appear self-

events.name: Hana
events.text: I survived by judgment, not luck. Every step I chose kept me alive. I'm here to win, not to owe anyone.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus betrayed Ash despite their pact and ignored Bex's drowning. Hana also abandoned Bex, but Gus's deliberate pact break is worse; question Hana for accountability.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: You watched Bex drown despite owing her a life debt. Why should the jury reward your judgment over someone else's betrayal?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Fenn's question targets my debt to Bex and my inaction. I must justify saving myself was rational, not betrayal, and that my judgment earned survival.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I owed Bex, but drowning alongside her wouldn't honor that debt. My judgment preserved a finalist who can vote wisely.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana's plea was weak, focusing on judgment over honoring debts. She admits she owed Bex but chose not to save her, which is a significant point for the jury. I will question her on this specific choice to highlight her self-serving nature.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Hana, you watched Bex drown despite owing her a life debt. Why should the jury reward your judgment over someone else's betrayal?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Cole is testing if I regret not saving Bex. I need to justify my survival as strategic, not cowardly, and remind jurors of my judgment without attacking Bex.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I owed Bex, but dying with her wouldn't repay the debt. Staying alive lets me honor her by making the best final choice.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus broke his pact with Ash by voting him; Hana let Bex drown despite a life debt. Eli broke with Ash explicitly but openly. Gus deserves scrutiny.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, you voted Ash while bound by pact, then claimed you honored pacts. Explain why the jury should trust your word.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara questions Ash pact betrayal; clarify it ended before vote, emphasize honored active pacts with Bex/Hana to rebuild trust.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash pact ended when Bex broke hers first by voting Ash out. I honored active pacts with Bex then Hana. Trust my word on that.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus lied about honoring pacts with me, and Hana let me drown despite my life debt. I want to expose Eli's 'I honored every pact' claim by forcing him to explain why he broke his Ash pact.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli, you claimed to honor every pact yet explicitly broke yours with Ash. Why should the jury trust your integrity over Gus?

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex is dead and bitter. I need to reframe: my pact with Ash was broken by circumstance, not malice. Gus also broke pacts but spins better. I must admit tactical necessity without sounding ruthless. The jury values survival honesty over false nobility.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash and I were bound, but Bex's actions shattered that alliance structure. I adapted to survive, not to deceive. Gus broke pacts too; the difference

events.name: Ash
events.text: As a juror I want to probe the finalist whose record is least clear. Gus voted out Ash while bound by a pact and his answer shifted blame; Eli also broke a pact explicitly. Hana's answers about Bex were consistent. I'll question Gus on the vote against Ash.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, you voted Ash while holding a pact with him. Did you ever intend to honor that pact, or was it only useful until then?

events.name: Gus
events.text: Ash's question aims to paint me as a betrayer; stress pact was mutual and broke due to Bex's betrayal first to justify my vote and gain jury favor.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Intended to honor Ash pact while it served us both. Bex broke hers first by voting you, voiding ours. Adapted to survive as all did.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to craft a closing statement that secures jury votes. Fenn and Cole died on bridge/glass—Gus's domain. Dara died to crusher—no finalist blame. Bex and Ash died to pit and vote. I have pacts with Hana and Gus still recorded, showing loyalty. I adapted but didn't initiate be

events.name: Eli
events.text: I kept my pact with Hana intact to the end. I never cast the first vote against a partner; I adapted when Bex and Gus

events.name: Gus
events.text: Final closing; affirm pacts honored until betrayals forced adaptation, highlight survival strategy without excuses to sway jury.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Honored pacts while mutual. Betrayals by others forced survival moves. Played smart, stayed loyal when possible. Vote for consistent Gus.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I need to present myself as loyal and honorable to the jury, while subtly distancing from Eli and Gus who have broken pacts. My closing should highlight my consistent survival without burning bridges.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I honor my debts and pacts; I never broke a vote or a promise. I made hard choices to survive, but always with integrity. I

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Hana preserved her survival without pretending loyalty; Eli strategically broke Ash's pact, while Gus openly betrayed Ash and defended it inconsistently.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli's claim of adapting to survive is weak, especially after Bex's death. Gus's consistent, albeit self-serving, approach to pacts and survival makes him a more reliable player. Hana's integrity claims ring hollow given Bex's fate. I rank Gus highest for strategic consistency, El

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus voted pact-partner Ash; Eli explicitly broke his Ash pact; Hana's record shows no broken pact or broken vote.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus betrayed Ash while holding a pact with him, showing disloyalty; Hana maintained her pacts and integrity throughout the game.
